definition: Arranged in a flat-topped or gently rounded flower cluster, with the lower stalks longer so that the blossoms reach much the same level.
etymology: It comes through Latin corymbus from Greek korymbos, a word for a cluster or tuft—especially one like ivy’s. Botanists kept the image and gave it to flowers that gather themselves into a little floral canopy.
usage: The last yarrow along the lane stood corymbose and pale against the September grass.
